decision: Read-only CDC purge readiness audit before implementing cleanup
scope: SQL Server CDC change-table retention; no business-table deletion or application decommissioning
decisions: Inspect all six configured capture instances, including the archive-only lab probe. Keep the five-table warehouse consumer contract explicit.
Observe a fixed upper LSN, enumerate bounded retained CDC row identities, and re-read the same bounded source observation afterward. LSN numeric gaps are not treated as missing events.

Read and checksum every active archive manifest and payload, compare in-scope manifest hashes and counts with sales/v2 batch acknowledgements, and compare post-bootstrap business streaming event semantic hashes with the warehouse ledger. Probe-only batches remain archive-only; mixed batches with business rows require warehouse acknowledgement.
Expand each Debezium update into SQL CDC before/after image identities and preserve multiplicity. Deduplicate identical archive redeliveries by event identity; conflicting copies block readiness.
Distinguish pre-bootstrap CDC history from the initial snapshot. Snapshot state does not prove that earlier changes can be replayed.
Use a 72-hour initial lab retention margin, matching the source cleanup job's initial 4,320-minute setting. Production retention and consumer ownership remain unapproved.

Provision distinct SQL Server, PostgreSQL and S3 audit identities. SQL access cannot delete changes or execute cleanup; PostgreSQL permits only the needed ledger/metadata reads; S3 permits only archive reads/listing.
Run one bounded 512 MiB/1 CPU container on demand, with a protected read-only source observation. No permanent service, Airflow purge task, cleanup executable or destructive schedule is installed.
Always emit purge_authorized=false and executable_low_watermark=null. Missing evidence is unknown, never implicitly successful.
Retain per-run source observations, policy hashes, code hashes, diagnostics and a root-protected report; an unsuccessful audit does not replace the last completed report.
required_follow_up_before_cleanup_implem: Reconcile all source CDC column values, not only retained identities and multiplicity.
Certify a durable connector resume checkpoint and a complete source transaction fence; maximum observed LSN alone is insufficient.
Account for retained changes from before bootstrap and every other CDC consumer.
Approve retention, consumer ownership and the rollback/replay contract.
Prove archive and checkpoint restoration outside the source VM.

Design a separate bounded executor that revalidates capture-instance identity and cleanup boundaries immediately before action, records partial outcomes and handles low-watermark advancement even when physical deletion fails.
limits: At most 100,000 retained CDC rows per capture instance in this first observer; exceeding the bound aborts instead of truncating evidence. Larger histories require partitioned reconciliation.
Warehouse batch acknowledgements establish the loader's transaction record; initial snapshot row semantics are not fully recomputed by this audit.
Source identity matching does not certify every source column or transaction atomicity.
The report is an operator diagnostic, not a signed authorization token for future deletion.
The single-VM and trusted-network lab limitations remain.
